messages:
Alex: Heads-up: p95 decode spiked ~30% on main after yesterday's optimizer merge (PR #432). Noticed during canary. Traces point to attention transpose kernel taking extra time, and KV cache hit pattern looks off. Perf CI also landed a regression :grimacing:
Priya: ugh. which perf job? can you paste the job link and exact build id?
Alex: perf job: https://perf.ci/reports/174985 - job id 2026-03-18_03:22. Build: runtime-6f3b9e6
Alex: quick flame snippet from the canary run:
```
  other                       0.0ms
  fused_attention_transpose  12.3ms
  kv_cache_lookup             9.6ms
```
Marco: that's from the new tiling optimizer landed in runtime/opt. I saw small local microbench diffs but nothing like +30%. Did the merge change KV key layout or memcpy boundaries?
Kara: I repro'd on a local canary with long sequences (seq=2048). KV load path shows misaligned memcpy and a fallback branch that wasn't present before. Trace: https://traces.internal/trace/abc-174985
Priya: can you bisect to isolate the commit range? we need the exact culprit for rollback vs fix decision
Alex: started bisect: `git bisect start; good=origin/main~50; bad=HEAD`. Narrowed to merge commit 6f3b9e6 (runtime/opt: transpose tiling rewrite) as first bad.
Marco: confirmed locally. 6f3b9e6 introduces `tile_width` heuristics and a conditional small-tile path. That path seems to be chosen for medium batch/long-seq combos and is slower due to extra branchy logic.
Kara: quick workaround: set env `RW_TILE_LEGACY=1` to force previous tiling. Canary with that env drops p95 back to baseline. Repro script: `./eng/tools/repro_longseq.sh --seq 2048`
perf-ci-bot: perf job runtime/main/2026-03-18 reported p95 +31% vs baseline (threshold 10%).
deploy-bot: Canary deploy v1.23.1 -> flagged, automatic rollback triggered (v1.23.0).
Priya: ok. Marco, can you prepare a revert or a targeted tweak to the tiling heuristic? If a quick revert lands, we can unblock the release. Otherwise propose rollout hold and revert in next patch.
Marco: I'll open a revert PR against runtime @ in ~30m unless I can land a narrow fix. The hotspot is in `tile_select()` where the small-tile branch takes effect for width < 64.
Alex: I'll attach the perf diffs, traces, and the canary repro to the PR. Also adding microbench test to catch this: long-seq + kv-alignment assertion.
Kara: logs copied to /tmp/trace-174985.log and repro script added to `eng/tools`. I also captured raw nvprof output in `artifacts/nvprof-174985.tar.gz`.
Priya: also let's add a CI perf guard that runs the long-seq repro in node-level perf suite to avoid regressions in merges.
Alex: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/439 (revert/tiling-optimizer). Will ping when CI completes. :thumbsup:
Marco: thanks. if revert lands, we should unfreeze canary and run a compare.
Alex: agreed. will follow up with p95 numbers once canary finishes.
Kara: FYI I dumped kv keys alignment in the repro: `xxd -g 4 -c 32 kv_dump.bin | head` — looks like 8-byte shift on some shards.
Priya: great debugging. keep notes in the PR description so support/sre can link postmortem if needed.
